revisions.reason: Retain Chrysostom’s saving-love interpretation and add John Paul II’s account of the Cross opening and correcting reason.
Preserves the Song’s human and spiritual readings while adding Benedict’s account of embodied desire maturing into care.
Adds the Eucharist’s transforming relation to bodily daily worship, retaining the existing meaning of willing self-offering.
Makes the existing received-gift insight more practically demanding: Christian generosity includes receiving love, rather than imagining oneself inexhaustible.
Retain the distinction between testing work, purification and condemnation; add Benedict’s explicitly attributed reflection on the saving encounter with Christ.
Preserve trust, Abraham and suffering while adding Benedict’s account of faith as a real beginning of the future promised by God, without asserting a disputed lexical definition.
Retain responsible speech and add Benedict’s complementary insistence that love needs truth about the human good, not merely sincerity or agreeable feeling.
Preserve Augustine’s accessible starting point while adding the papal distinction between a gift and what is already owed in justice.
Preserve resurrection, intercession and the Eucharist; add Benedict’s explanation that shared lives and love make prayer for the dead intelligible.
Add the distinction between indispensable organised care and personal compassion, preserving the original neighbour-making insight.
Deepen the existing mercy/conversion note through John Paul II’s explicit distinction between restoration of dignity and humiliating pity.
Retain the priority of divine love and the real response of faith, adding John Paul II’s direct application of this verse to human self-understanding.
Preserve the sacramental memorial and complete sacrifice, specifying the present responsibility generated by Eucharistic expectation of Christ’s return.
Keep the completeness of Christ’s sacrifice while adding the papal reading of suffering persons as participants rather than merely burdens or recipients of care.
